newsitem.title: USA: Cleveland airport expansion agreement finalized.
newsitem.headline: Cleveland airport expansion agreement finalized.

text.p: A pact between Cleveland and one of its neighboring cities over the expansion of Cleveland Hopkins International Airport has been finalized, Cleveland Mayor Michael White announced Monday.

The city's agreement with Brook Park, a city that borders the airport, clears the way for passage of authorizing legislation by the governing councils of the two cities, according to a news release from White's office.

"This is the day I have been anticipating for many years, the day when the negotiations are complete and the expansion can begin 00 expansion to provide more facilities for the traveling public and more jobs for the citizens of the Cleveland metropolitan area," White said.

The agreement calls for an exchange of land and money between the two cities in order to accomodate a runway project that is part of a $500 million, five-year airport expansion plan. White and Brook Park Mayor Thomas Coyne had announced a tentative agreement in August.
White's news release said authorizing legislation for the pact will be introduced Monday night to the Cleveland City Council.

Contruction on a new 6,450-foot runway is expected to be completed in late 1999. An airport official has said the runway project would be financed with general airport revenue bonds and federal aviation grants.
